result:
I put the answer in `final.py`. It scores **0.5833 on the search split**, against 0.365 for LRU, and I used **15 of the 24 scorer calls**.

I left 9 calls unspent. In the last rounds, every candidate my local harness rated was within ±0.001 of the final pick, and spending calls on ties like that would mostly fit the search split rather than the unseen traces. The final pick was confirmed with a scorer call, but there is no held-out run on the scorer: the unseen-trace score is only taken later. In its place I used seeds on my local harness that I never tuned on.

| | search split (scorer) | held-out seeds (my harness) |
|---|---|---|
| LRU baseline | 0.365 | 0.298 |
| First strong single policy (W-TinyLFU) | 0.533 | 0.333 |
| Best single policy (LIRS) | 0.566 | 0.380 |
| **Final (`final.py`)** | **0.583** | **0.406** |

**Why it beats LRU:** each type of access pattern has a different best policy, so `final.py` runs five policies side by side on the same requests and follows whichever has been hitting most lately:
- **LRU and ARC** are best on the recency-heavy traces (0.85 on the scorer's "recency" trace).
- **W-TinyLFU** is best on hot keys mixed with loops.
- **S3-FIFO** does well on traces that switch phases and resist one-off scans.
- **A policy I wrote that predicts when each key will come back** keeps the key expected back soonest. It evicts keys that are well past their expected return first, and it learns how often brand-new keys ever return. On loops bigger than the cache it keeps a fixed part of the loop, which raised "shifting_loops" from 0.16 (ARC) to 0.85. On its own it was the strongest single policy on my harness.

A policy only takes over once its decayed hit count beats the current leader's by 5%. Without that margin it flipped back and forth between two near-tied policies and lost 0.11 on "loop_and_hot". The real cache then copies the leader gradually: it evicts the key the leader just dropped, and it only stores a new key the leader also holds. That way it never adds anything but the requested key and never holds more than `capacity`. Making each policy report the key it just evicted cut the run time by 2.2×. My harness's 30 traces of 30,000 requests take about 2.7s, well inside the 8-second limit.

**Families tried:**

| Approach | Result |
|---|---|
| ARC | 0.407 on its own |
| W-TinyLFU | 0.533 on its own |
| W-TinyLFU with a self-tuning window | 0.529: better on recency, worse on loops |
| S3-FIFO | 0.462 on its own |
| LIRS | 0.566 on its own, the best single policy |
| Return-time predictor | strongest on my harness |
| LFU with aging, hyperbolic caching | weak, dropped |
| Experts voting on what to keep | worse than following one leader, dropped |
| Predictor variants: deadline heap, skipping keys predicted back last, frequency gate | no gain, dropped |
